page: Amazon Web Services c6i.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core via Hyper-Threading. It includes 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU acceleration, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core performance alongside constrained multi-core and memory capabilities. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance achieves an average rating of 1881.49, while multi-core performance drops to a poor rating of 1922.07. Similarly, Geekbench scores show an average single-core result of 1622.0 but a poor multi-core result of 1856.0. Memory bandwidth is limited, with large-block read and write speeds registering at 14.26 GB/sec and 13.09 GB/sec respectively, both falling into the bottom 10% tier. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression (27.86 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (10.26 GB/sec) perform at average levels.

The c6i.large offers a dedicated compute profile at a low entry-level resource scale, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but do not demand high memory capacity or multi-threaded throughput. However, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and low memory bandwidth represent significant tradeoffs, as evidenced by poor performance in database operations (1015.57 on Passmark) and Redis SET operations (1.91 million operations/sec). This instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic web serving, or small-scale batch processing where memory footprint and multi-core scaling are not primary bottlenecks.
